stem: What does the Wyoming act show about women's changing place in the West?

stimulus.source_note: An Act to Grant to the Women of Wyoming Territory the Right of Suffrage and to Hold Office, approved December 10, 1869. Public domain. Text verified against the American Battlefield Trust transcription (from the Library of Congress) and History of Woman Suffrage, vol. 3.
stimulus.text:
An Act to Grant to the Women of Wyoming Territory the Right of Suffrage and to Hold Office, approved December 10, 1869:

"SECTION 1. That every woman of the age of twenty-one years, residing in this territory, may, at every election to be holden under the laws thereof, cast her vote. And her rights to the elective franchise and to hold office shall be the same under the election laws of the territory, as those of electors."

"SECTION 2. This act shall take effect and be in force from and after its passage."

options.text: Western women had already won the vote everywhere by 1869
options.misconception: Background: Wyoming was first; most western states followed later, and the nation waited until 1920.

options.text: Western women played no part in public life before 1869
options.misconception: Background: western women already ran farms, taught school, and kept settlements going before any law recognized them.

options.text: The West, where women's labor was visible, moved toward equality first
The act ended all legal limits on women in the territory
options.misconception: Background: the act covered voting and office-holding, not every legal limit.

rationales.A: Background: Wyoming was first. Most western states followed later, and the nation waited until 1920.
rationales.B: Background: western women already ran farms, taught school, and kept settlements going before any law recognized them.
rationales.C: Background: farm women worked the fields, kept the books, and held isolated households together, and western territories rewarded that visible work with the vote, Wyoming first in 1869, other western states following before the East.
rationales.D: Background: the act covered voting and office-holding, not every legal limit.
rationales.general:
Picture a farm wife who ploughs, teaches, nurses, and keeps the books, miles from any neighbor.
1. Ask what the East saw of such women. Background: Little, because eastern women worked inside homes and shops.
2. Ask what the West saw. Background: Labor that held whole settlements together, out in the open.
3. Name the pattern. Background: Where women's work was visible and essential, the vote followed first.
Remember: equality often starts as recognition, a law catching up with work already done.
